HYPOTHESIS (natural language, grounded in the executed numbers):
In the PCA on the forms of capital in hundred-year time slices, the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age is a pronounced positive outlier. PC1 at 1100 BCE (+4.447 in the primary full-series PCA) exceeds every subsequent horizon of 1000–500 BCE — by about +2.3 units versus 1000 BCE and by +2.6 to +3.7 units versus the 900–500 BCE slices — and is roughly 3.0 units above the 1000–500 BCE mean (+1.412). From 1000 BCE onward PC1 declines steadily, reaching its YBA minimum at 600–500 BCE (~+0.78). Thus the Younger Bronze Age does not begin with low capital accumulation that grows: it opens at a peak of accumulated "capital" (hoards/depots, copper–gold, daggers, large houses, monuments) that collapses sharply after 1100 BCE and is never regained during 1000–500 BCE. PC1 loads positively on the prestige/wealth indicators (ZCU_AU +0.78, ZHort +0.65, ZDolch +0.51, Zhausgr +0.43, ZMonument +0.39, ZAxtSchwert +0.57), so the high 1100 BCE score is driven by a short-lived spike in hoarding and metal wealth (ZCU_AU +2.85, ZHort 3.38, ZDolch +1.10, Zhausgr +1.65, ZMonument +1.35 at 1100 BCE) followed by their rapid decline, while routine-agricultural indicators (sickles, axes/celts, pottery form) stay flat or low.

EXECUTED WORKFLOW:
1. Loaded data/capital.csv (39 rows, one per 100-year slice, BCE 500–4300; all 12 Z-columns 100% populated). Verified each row equals the corresponding annual row of time_series_data.csv at CE = −BCE (raw and interpolated values coincide at the slice marks).
2. Variance check on the full 39-row table: NO variable had zero/near-zero variance (min var = ZSichel 0.289, ZMW 0.974, ZHort 0.974; all others ≈1.0) — nothing excluded in the primary PCA (stated explicitly per your condition 1).
3. Primary PCA (approved design): all 12 Z-indicators, standardized across the 39 rows (correlation-matrix equivalent), fit on the FULL table, then PC1 read off at the YBA slices. PC1 explains 30.3% of variance. Sign convention fixed and stated: PC1 oriented so the ZHort loading is positive (higher PC1 = more capital; ZCU_AU loading is also positive under this convention).
4. PC1 by YBA century slice (primary, full-table fit): 1100 BCE = +4.447; 1000 = +2.148; 900 = +1.627; 800 = +1.894; 700 = +1.225; 600 = +0.800; 500 = +0.779. 1100 minus mean of 1000–500 = +3.035; 1100 is above every later slice by +2.299 (1000) to +3.669 (500).
5. Sensitivity (YBA-only PCA, rows 1100–500): within the YBA window ZSichel and ZKeform have zero variance and were explicitly excluded (10 variables retained). PC1 explains 62.5% of variance. PC1(1100) = +5.349 vs later mean = −0.892 (diff +6.241), with 1100 above every later slice. The 1100-vs-later comparison HOLDS in direction and magnitude class in both variants.
6. Pollen file (Belau/Woserin openness PCA) was kept out of the computation as agreed — it is a separate land-cover/openness PCA, not the forms-of-capital PCA.

PC1 LOADINGS (primary, full-table fit, sign-fixed):
ZCU_AU +0.777, Zkeverz +0.729, ZHort +0.648, ZAxtSchwert +0.570, ZDolch +0.507, ZMW +0.461, Zhausgr +0.429, ZMonument +0.390, ZSichel −0.285, Zamber −0.456, ZBeil −0.461, ZKeform −0.673.

LIMITATIONS / UNCERTAINTIES:
- PC1 sign is arbitrary; the fixed convention (ZHort>0 ⇒ higher PC1 = more capital) makes the direction unambiguous, but the "more capital" interpretation rests on the loading pattern.
- PCA fit set choice matters quantitatively (full-table +3.0 vs YBA-only +6.2 difference) but not qualitatively; 1100 BCE is an outlier in both.
- Zkeverz (pottery decoration) loads positively on PC1, which is not a classic "capital" indicator; the component is best read as a general wealth/prestige-intensity axis.
- 1100 BCE is a single 100-year slice; the spike could partly reflect one-time depositional events (e.g., hoards) rather than sustained wealth.

payload.hypothesis: In the PCA on the forms of capital in hundred-year time slices, the Younger Bronze Age opens at a pronounced peak rather than a low point: PC1 at 1100 BCE (+4.447) lies about 3.0 units above the mean of the 1000–500 BCE slices (+1.412) and exceeds every subsequent horizon by +2.3 to +3.7 units, then declines monotonically-ish to ~+0.8 by 600–500 BCE. With PC1 oriented so higher values mean more capital (positive loadings on copper–gold +0.78, depots/hoards +0.65, daggers +0.51, house size +0.43, monuments +0.39), the 1100 BCE outlier is driven by a short-lived spike in hoarding and metal wealth (ZCU_AU +2.85, ZHort 3.38, ZDolch +1.10, Zhausgr +1.65, ZMonument +1.35 at 1100 BCE) that collapses from 1000 BCE onward; routine-agricultural indicators (sickles, axes/celts, pottery form) remain flat or low. A YBA-only PCA sensitivity (excluding the YBA-invariant ZSichel and ZKeform) reproduces the same pattern with even larger contrast (PC1(1100) = +5.35 vs later mean −0.89), confirming that the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age represents a high point of accumulated capital not sustained through 1000–500 BCE.
payload.workflow: Loaded capital.csv (39 century rows, BCE 500-4300); variance-checked all 12 Z-indicators (none zero-variance in full table; ZSichel and ZKeform constant within YBA and excluded only in the YBA-only sensitivity); standardized and ran correlation-matrix PCA via numpy SVD on the full 39-row table as primary; fixed PC1 sign so ZHort loading is positive (higher PC1 = more capital); extracted PC1 at 1100, 1000, 900, 800, 700, 600, 500 BCE; computed the 1100-vs-1000-500 difference (+3.035) and per-slice differences (+2.30 to +3.67); repeated PCA on YBA rows only as sensitivity (+6.241, same direction); pollen openness file excluded from computation. Outputs: pc1_by_century.csv, pc1_loadings.csv.
